findings.description: The instance user_data exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in plain text. Anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute or access to the instance metadata can retrieve these long-lived credentials.
No metadata_options block is set, so IMDSv1 remains enabled and an SSRF flaw in the web application could be used to retrieve instance credentials without a token.
No root_block_device or ebs_block_device encryption is configured, so the instance's attached storage may be created unencrypted at rest.

The instance is placed in a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and a route to an internet gateway, giving it a public address and direct internet exposure combined with a wide-open security group.
Ingress on TCP port 22 is open to 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and exploitation attempts.
Ingress on TCP port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 serving unencrypted HTTP, meaning traffic to end users is not encrypted in transit.
Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted data exfiltration and command-and-control channel.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true (it is explicitly commented out), so data written to the volume is stored unencrypted.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted volume and no KMS encryption is configured, so the snapshot contents are stored unencrypted and can be shared or copied.
The VPC flow log destination bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so audit log data is stored unencrypted.
No public access block, bucket policy, or ACL restriction is defined for the flow log bucket, risking public or cross-account exposure of network audit logs.
The bucket that stores security audit data has no access logging or versioning enabled, so tampering with or deletion of flow logs would go undetected.
map_public_ip_on_launch is true, so every instance launched in this subnet receives a public IP address and is directly reachable from the internet rather than isolated in a private layer.
map_public_ip_on_launch is true, so instances launched in this subnet are automatically given public IPs and exposed to the internet.
The VPC's default security group is not explicitly restricted with an aws_default_security_group resource, so it retains its permissive default rules.
